title: Survival Analysis for Feature Lifespan Across Training Checkpoints

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Characterizing when safety-relevant features emerge in training could inform when interpretability audits are most useful and whether late-emerging features pose special risks. The chain is plausible though requires further work to become actionable.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Survival analysis (Kaplan-Meier, lifelines library) is well-documented and accessible. Pre-trained SAEs on checkpoints are available. The main complexity is running SAEs across many checkpoints and defining birth/death thresholds, which requires some experimentation. Medium compute suffices.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Requires running SAEs on multiple training checkpoints, defining birth/death criteria, computing survival curves, and testing predictors. The checkpoint iteration is time-consuming but automatable. Tight but feasible in 30 hours if limited to one model family.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
